questions.question: Why do enterprise ASM programs use distributed scanning architectures?
options: A single machine cannot cover large asset inventories within useful timeframes, and distribution helps with scale, rate limits, and geographic coverage
Distributed scanning is always cheaper
It is a legal requirement for companies over 1000 employees
Single-node scanning produces inaccurate results
questions.explanation: At enterprise scale you're monitoring thousands of assets continuously. Distributing workers handles volume, respects per-source rate limits, and can scan from multiple network vantage points.

questions.question: What is a key data consideration when designing enterprise-scale ASM?
options: Storing everything in a single spreadsheet
Planning data flow, aggregation, and storage (e.g., ElasticSearch) before building, since scan volume grows quickly
Deleting all results after each scan
Avoiding databases to keep things simple
questions.explanation: Continuous scanning of a large estate produces large, growing datasets. Architecture work — data flow, aggregation, indexed storage like ElasticSearch/Kibana — must be planned up front.

questions.question: Why should an enterprise ASM platform expose API interfaces?
options: APIs are required to use Go-based tools
So other security systems (SIEM, ticketing, CMDB) can integrate with and act on ASM data
To allow the public to query your asset inventory
APIs make the platform run faster
questions.explanation: ASM data is most valuable when it flows into the rest of the security stack: SIEM correlation, automatic ticket creation, asset-inventory reconciliation. APIs enable that integration.

questions.question: Beyond monitoring targets, what does a production ASM platform itself need?
options: Monitoring and alerting for the platform's own health, so scanning failures don't create silent coverage gaps
A public status page
Daily manual restarts
A dedicated physical data center
questions.explanation: The watchers need watching: if scanners die or queues back up silently, you lose attack surface visibility without knowing it. Operational monitoring of the platform is essential.

questions.question: How do you demonstrate that an ASM architecture performs at scale?
options: By assuming it will work because the tools are popular
By load-testing the pipeline against realistic asset volumes and measuring throughput and completeness
By running it once against a single domain
By reading the tool documentation
questions.explanation: Scale claims need evidence: process realistic volumes, measure scan throughput, data pipeline latency, and result completeness, and find the bottlenecks before production does.
